headline: Snap spins off AI video team into new company Dotmo
summary: Snap's AI video team becomes separate company to focus on gaming experiences
details: Snap is spinning off an internal generative AI video team into a separate company called Dotmo. The new company will focus on developing AI models for interactive gaming experiences.

The high costs of conducting such work internally were cited as one of the reasons for the spinoff. Snap will provide Dotmo with a license to adapt its technology for gaming and interactive entertainment platforms.

Dotmo's initial team will consist of current Snap staff who are leaving Snap to launch the new venture. Snap's CTO, Bobby Murphy, will act as lead investor and have a significant personal stake in the new firm.

headline: Game Boy Camera now works with your phone connects via USB-C
summary: The Game Boy Camera can now be used with smartphones via USB-C. This new compatibility allows users to connect and utilize the camera with their mobile devices.
details: The Game Boy Camera, a nostalgic gadget from the 90s, has gained compatibility with modern smartphones. Users can now connect the camera to their phones using a USB-C cable.

This new feature enables users to take photos and possibly use the camera in various apps. The Game Boy Camera originally released as a peripheral for the Game Boy, allowing users to take pixelated photos.
The compatibility update breathes new life into the retro camera, making it possible for users to integrate it with their current mobile devices.
caption:
Can you use a 90s camera with your smartphone?

The Game Boy Camera, a nostalgic gadget from the 90s, has gained compatibility with modern smartphones. Users can now connect the camera to their phones using a USB-C cable.
